sections.title: The Reformation of Josiah
observations: King Josiah, upon discovering the Book of the Law, initiates a significant religious reform in Judah. This discovery highlights the importance of Scripture in guiding the life of God's people.
Josiah's actions demonstrate a sincere desire to return to the covenantal obligations set forth by God, showcasing the transformative power of God's Word when it is rediscovered and applied.

sections.title: The Removal of Idolatry
observations: Josiah's reforms include the removal of idolatrous practices and the destruction of pagan altars, which reflects a commitment to purity in worship.
This section emphasizes the necessity of removing anything that distracts from true worship of God, illustrating the seriousness with which God views idolatry.

sections.title: The Passover Celebration
observations: The reinstatement of the Passover is a pivotal moment, as it signifies a return to the foundational practices of Israel's faith.
This celebration not only honors God's deliverance but also serves as a communal act of remembrance and obedience, reinforcing the identity of God's people.

importantVerses.commentary: Josiah reads the Book of the Law to the people, signifying the importance of Scripture in the life of the community.
There was no king like Josiah who turned to the Lord with all his heart, soul, and might, highlighting the depth of his commitment to God.
Josiah commands the people to keep the Passover, emphasizing the importance of remembering God's deliverance.

questions: What does Josiah's response to the discovery of the Book of the Law teach us about the importance of Scripture in our lives today?
How can we apply the lessons of removing idolatry from our lives in a modern context?
In what ways does the celebration of Passover connect to our understanding of salvation and remembrance in the New Testament?
